overview.description: Belote is the national card game of France, a 32-card partnership trick-taking game descended from the Jass family. It is renowned for its unique trump ranking system where the Jack ('J' or 'Valet') and the 9 ('Neuf') become the two most powerful cards, dwarfing the Ace. Players bid to establish a trump suit, declare melds ('Tierce', 'Quarte'), and strive to reach 501 or 1000 points. The term 'Belote' specifically refers to the King and Queen of Trumps held together, a declaration that can swing the game.

history.origins: Believed to be derived from the Dutch game 'Klaverjas', brought to France by diamond merchants or Jewish communities in the early 20th century.
timeline: 1914: Becomes popular among French soldiers (Poilus) in WWI trenches.
1920s: Establishes itself as the dominant café game in Paris, overtaking Manille.
Present: The most played card game in France with a codified federation (FFB).
history.evolution: The game evolved into 'Belote Contrée' and 'Coinche' where bidding is more strategic, but classic Belote remains the foundation.
history.cultural: In France, 'Une petite Belote?' is a standard social invitation. The nuances of signalling and the 'Dix de Der' (10 points for the last trick) are ingrained in French culture.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.equipment: Standard 32-card French pack (Piquet deck), score pad.
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards to each player (3-2). One card is turned face up (The Proposal). Players bid to take it as trump. If all pass, a second round of bidding allows naming any other suit. Remaining cards are dealt (3 each) for a total of 8.

rules.objective: The contracting team must score more points than the defenders (usually > 81 points out of 162 total). First team to 501 or 1000 wins the match.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding**: Accept turned trump or call another suit. 2. **Declarations**: Announced during the first trick. Only the team with the highest declaration scores theirs. 3. **The Play**: Forehand leads. Must follow suit. If void, must trump (unless partner winning). Must over-trump if trumps are led. 4. **Scoring**: Sum card points + declarations + 'Dix de Der' (10 bonus).
keyRules: The Jack of Trumps is the boss card (20 pts). The 9 of Trumps is the second boss (14 pts).
Strict trumping rules: You cannot undercut/under-trump unless forced.
Melds (Declarations) are only valid if they are better than the opponents' best meld.

strategy.basic: Count trumps (there are 8). When you have the 'Master' (Jack), draw trumps out immediately. Don't bid unless you have at least the Jack or the 9-Ace combo.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Impasse' (Finesse): Leading a low card through the opponent to trap their King/Queen if your partner holds the Ace/10. Trapping the 10 is crucial as it's worth 10 points.
strategy.advanced: Signaling (Appel): Discarding an Ace on a partner's winning trick signals 'I have the 10 or King, lead this suit again'. Or discarding a 7 asks for a suit change.
tips: Never under-lead an Ace in a non-trump suit unless you want to lose it.
Remember the Jack and 9 of trumps possess over 20% of the deck's point value.

list.name: Belote Coinchée
list.description: All cards are dealt at once. Players bid for points (e.g., '100 Spades') instead of simple acceptance. Opponents can 'Coinche' (Double).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation rules for bidding, doubling, and scoring are described but not yet mapped into structured engine overrides.

list.name: Belote Découverte
list.description: Open-hand variant for 2 players. 6 cards in hand, 6 face-up on table.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Layout, exposed-card structure, and two-player flow are documented but corresponding engine overrides have not yet been encoded.

difficulty.easy: Follows suit legally. Plays declarations if held. Doesn't track trumps.
difficulty.medium: Bids conservatively (needs J+9). Leads trumps to clear opponents. Attempts simple finesses.
difficulty.hard: Perfect Trump Count. Calculates 'Capot' (Winning all tricks) probability. Signals partner via discards. Sacrifices high cards to save the 'Dix de Der'.

considerations: Trump hierarchy inversion (J, 9 > A, 10) is the main logic hurdle.
Must track declarations to map missing high cards in the deck.

additional: French Federation of Belote (FFB) Official Rules

ante.reason: Belote is a point-based partnership game and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante.

deal.reason: The two-part distribution of cards and the turning of the trump proposal are handled by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: The trump proposal card is public, but there is no shared community market of playable cards in this game.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase cards from any market area; cards are obtained only through the system-managed deal.

buy_stock.reason: The entire deck is exhausted during the two-part deal phase; no cards remain in stock to be purchased during play.

fold.reason: Players are committed to their partnership's participation and must play through all eight tricks of the hand.

check.reason: The game uses a trick-taking structure rather than a vying structure where checking would be an appropriate action.

call.reason: There is no pot to match in classic Belote; competition is based on card point values and melds.

bet.reason: Success is determined by total point accumulation on a scorecard rather than through financial or chip betting.

raise.reason: The value of the deal is fixed by the game rules and cannot be raised through wagering rounds.

declare.description: Declare melds (Tierce, Quarte, Belote) during the first trick.
declare.constraints: Must be leading or playing to the first trick.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private until individual cards are played into tricks; no full-hand reveal phase occurs.

award_pot.reason: Winning points are added to a cumulative session total rather than distributed from a physical pot.

play_card.description: Play a card to the trick; follow suit and trump rules.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit; must trump if void; must over-trump if possible.

draw.reason: All cards are distributed during the two-part deal; no drawing phase exists during the play of the tricks.

discard.reason: Every card in the player's hand must be played into a trick; no cards are discarded or buried.

pass.description: Pass during the trump selection phase.
pass.constraints: Allowed when choosing not to accept the proposed trump suit.

bid.reason: Trump selection is performed via a simple acceptance check rather than a competitive bidding auction.

meld.description: Declare sequences or groups for bonus points during the first trick.
meld.constraints: Only the best meld at the table is awarded points.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates only after all eight tricks have been played by all participants.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Cards are distributed in two fixed dealing rounds; no draw pile exists during trick play.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played directly to tricks; no separate waste or discard pile is utilized.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Certain ranks (Jack and 9) have high point values in trumps but do not trigger automated engine effects.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Trump selection is performed openly via verbal acceptance; no hidden tokens are used.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Belote is a trick-taking game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Goal is to reach target points via tricks and melds; hands are played out in tricks, not emptied as in shedding games.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Must over-trump if possible when trumps are played.

customActions.description: Distribute five cards to each player and turn one card for the trump proposal.
Accept the turned card as the trump suit for the hand.
Distribute the remaining three cards to each player once trump is established.
Play a card to the trick and optionally announce a meld.
Sum card points, melds, and last-trick bonus to determine round winner.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; card value comparison (Jack of trumps is highest) determines trick winner.
engine.deckDescription: One standard 32-card deck: eight ranks (seven through ace) in each of four French suits. No jokers; used for Belote where the jack and nine of trump are the two highest cards and marriages score bonus points.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Trump is determined by the turned card or bidding; follow suit when able. The jack (belote) and nine of trump outrank all other trumps.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit: seven, eight, nine, ten, jack, queen, king, ace. In trump order: jack highest, then nine, ace, ten, king, queen, eight, seven. In plain suits: ace, ten, king, queen, jack, nine, eight, seven. Point values as in Belote.
engine.dealPattern: Initial deal of 5 cards (3 then 2), then a final deal of 3 cards.

hero.title: BELOTE
hero.subtitle: La France aux Cartes
hero.tagline: Jack is Master. Nine is Vice. Ace is just a spectator.

synthesis.shortDescription: France's beloved national pastime. A strategic 32-card duel where the Jack of Trumps reigns supreme. Bid smart, declare your marriages (Belote-Rebelote), and fight for every ten-point card to avoid the dreaded 'Dedans'.

prompts.human: The turned card is the Jack of Diamonds. That's 20 points instantly! You hold the 9 and Ace of Diamonds too. Take it! You have the Top 3 Trumps ('Trente-Quatre'). Declare 'Tierce' on the first trick for bonus points.
prompts.ai: Game: Belote. Type: Jass/Trick-Taking. Rules: J(20)>9(14)>A(11)>10(10). Must follow, Must Trump if void. 162 total points. Belote=K+Q of trump.

scoring.winCondition: First team to 501 (short game) or 1000 (long game) points.

penalties.Dix de Der: Winning the last (8th) trick awards a 10-point bonus.
penalties.Capot: Winning all eight tricks awards a total of 252 points.

scoring.splitRules: If points are tied (81-81), the contractor's points are 'Hanging' (Litige) and awarded to the winner of the next deal.
